issues.description: Method addGuestStudents(int): The problem statement's UML explicitly declares addGuestStudents(int) with return type void (problem_statement.md UML line), while the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) defines public boolean addGuestStudents(int). The template file contains only a TODO for adding this method (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java). This mismatch of return type (void vs boolean) creates an inconsistent contract: students reading the UML will implement a void method, but the solution (and any tests written against it) use a boolean return value, which can cause compilation failures or test mismatches and confuses students about the expected signature and semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addGuestStudents(int) signature consistent across artifacts. Two valid options: (A) Change the solution implementation to match the UML and problem text by making addGuestStudents(int) return void (remove boolean return and adjust implementation accordingly), and update any tests to expect void; or (B) Update the problem statement UML and task description to declare addGuestStudents(int) as returning boolean and document its semantics (e.g., returns true on success, false on invalid input), and update the template TODO and any tests to expect the boolean signature. Ensure the chosen signature is reflected consistently in the problem statement, template, solution, and tests.
